run.question:
Alertmanager alert RequestErrorRate (severity warning) is firing for service otel-demo/frontend-proxy since 2026-11-16T12:41:36Z.
Investigate why this alert is firing.

report.summary: The RequestErrorRate warning for otel-demo/frontend-proxy is explained by error spans that frontend-proxy itself recorded. Its 'ingress' spans returned HTTP 503 in a steady trickle (roughly 1-10 error spans per 5 minutes) from 12:11:30Z through at least 12:45:27Z, and its 'router frontend egress' spans carry error='true' with http.status_code='0'. The frontend-proxy (envoy) access log names the mechanism exactly: HTTP 503 with response code details 'UC upstream_reset_before_response_started{connection_termination}' toward the upstream cluster 'frontend'. In sampled traces the frontend service produced no span at all for those failed requests, so the upstream connection died before the frontend responded. The single frontend pod (frontend-675fd7b5c5-chsmw) is Running/Ready with restartCount 0 and about 125 MiB of a 200Mi limit, but it is chronically CPU-throttled (24-32% of CFS periods against a 100m limit) throughout the window. I found no crash, OOM, eviction, node pressure or readiness failure. The product-catalog pod replacement at 12:34:11Z was a manual rollout (kubectl restartedAt annotation, same image) and postdates the first 503 by 23 minutes. Which side actually closes the connection (frontend Node/Next server keep-alive close versus frontend-proxy's own upstream connection-pool handling) is unresolved: the frontend container's logs were empty in the window and the envoy config is baked into the image. The alert expression also cannot be verified: the RequestErrorRate rule is not loaded in the queried Prometheus, and the ingress error share I computed at 12:41:36 (~0.037%) does not reproduce the annotation's 0.01111111111111111.

claims.text: frontend-proxy span metrics for 11:41:36-13:01:45Z show STATUS_CODE_ERROR 34.44 spans versus STATUS_CODE_UNSET 56,621.73 spans (traces_span_metrics_calls_total); broken down by operation, the ERROR increases are 'ingress' 28.36 and 'router frontend egress' 6.08.

The frontend-proxy (envoy) access log records HTTP 503 responses with response code details 'UC upstream_reset_before_response_started{connection_termination}' for upstream cluster 'frontend' (endpoint 100.96.3.52), repeatedly from 2026-11-16T12:11:30.947Z through 2026-11-16T12:45:27.983Z; every sampled 503 line carries the same UC detail and the same 'frontend' upstream cluster.

In the sampled error traces, a request that received 503 carries a load-generator GET span with status 503/ERROR, a frontend-proxy 'ingress' span with status 503/ERROR, a frontend-proxy 'router frontend egress' span with error='true' and http.status_code='0', and no frontend service span; the whole trace b303e7616d6cc9296844951cbe4749d5 contains only those 4 spans.

The 5-minute ERROR increase on frontend-proxy 'ingress' ran at 0-5.6 per 5 minutes from 12:12:36 to 12:34:36, peaked at 10 (12:36:36) and 9.36 (12:38:36), then returned to 0-3.3 through 12:54:36; errors were still present after the 12:41:36Z alert start.

At the alert start instant 12:41:36Z the frontend-proxy 'ingress' spans in the preceding 5 minutes were ERROR 1.111 and UNSET 3021.11, an error share of about 0.037%, which does not match the alert annotation value 0.01111111111111111 (1.1%).

All 21 pods in namespace otel-demo were Running and Ready with restartCount 0 when checked, including frontend-675fd7b5c5-chsmw and frontend-proxy-6b4d584985-mzj56, and no container reported a lastState termination reason.

The frontend container's memory working set peaked at 130,908,160 bytes (~125 MiB) against a 200Mi limit, CPU usage stayed around 0.042-0.050 cores against a 100m limit, and its CFS-throttled period share was 24-32% at every 2-minute sample from 12:12:36 to 12:54:36.
The frontend-proxy container's CFS-throttled period share was 2.7-5.5% and its memory working set peaked at 21,143,552 bytes (~20 MiB) against a 50Mi limit.

The frontend service recorded its own ERROR spans in exactly one 5-minute bucket, 12:31:36-12:36:36Z: 'GET' 5.56, 'POST' 1.11, 'POST /api/checkout' 1.11, 'executing api route (pages) /api/checkout' 1.11 and 'tcp.connect' 1.11; all other 5-minute buckets in the window are 0 for these operations.
All five cluster nodes report Ready=True with MemoryPressure, DiskPressure, PIDPressure and NetworkUnavailable all False.

The frontend Deployment's ReplicaSet frontend-675fd7b5c5 (created 12:01:09Z) reports 1/1 ready/available, and frontend-proxy-6b4d584985 reports 1/1 ready/available; the frontend Service is clusterIP 100.71.221.228:8080 selecting opentelemetry.io/name=frontend, which matches that single pod.

Deployment otel-demo/product-catalog was rolled at 12:34:11-12:34:15Z from ReplicaSet product-catalog-7c7f8b68dc to product-catalog-55f64b54c9; the new ReplicaSet template carries kubectl.kubernetes.io/restartedAt=2026-11-16T12:34:11Z with the identical image ghcr.io/open-telemetry/demo:2.1.3-product-catalog and identical env vars and configmap volume.

Prometheus holds only traces-derived series for frontend-proxy (traces_span_metrics_calls_total and traces_span_metrics_duration_milliseconds_bucket); no http_* or rpc_* series exist for it in the queried window.

Crash, OOMKill, eviction and node pressure are not supported as causes: all otel-demo containers have restartCount 0 and no lastState termination, the only events in the namespace are 9 Normal product-catalog rollout events (Scheduled/Pulled/Created/Started/SuccessfulCreate/Killing/SuccessfulDelete/ScalingReplicaSet), and all nodes are Ready without memory, disk, PID or network pressure.

A frontend or frontend-proxy pod crash, OOMKill or restart-loop caused the 503s. Both pods report restartCount 0 with no lastState termination reason, no OOMKilled/Evicted/Unhealthy events exist in otel-demo, and memory working sets stay far below the configured limits.

The 12:34:11Z product-catalog rollout caused the frontend-proxy 503 stream. The first logged 503 is at 12:11:30.947Z, 23 minutes before the rollout, the 503s continue after it (12:40:08.72Z, 12:40:39.49Z, 12:45:27.98Z), and the rollout used the identical product-catalog image with a kubectl restartedAt marker.

The frontend pod's HTTP server terminates reused upstream connections before responding (for example a Node/Next.js keep-alive or idle-close racing envoy's connection pool). Evidence: envoy reports 'upstream_reset_before_response_started{connection_termination}' for the 'frontend' cluster and no frontend span exists for the failed requests, while the frontend Service selects only pod frontend-675fd7b5c5-chsmw. The frontend keep-alive settings and application logs could not be read, so this is unconfirmed.

frontend-proxy's own upstream connection-pool handling toward the frontend cluster (idle/drain/connection-limit behaviour) terminates the pooled connection; envoy emits the same UC 'connection_termination' detail in that case. The envoy configuration is baked into image ghcr.io/open-telemetry/demo:2.1.3-frontend-proxy and no frontend-proxy ConfigMap exists in the namespace, so this cannot be confirmed or excluded.

The frontend's chronic CPU constraint (24-32% of CFS periods throttled against a 100m limit, using about 0.045-0.05 cores) contributes to slow request handling and connection churn. It is only a correlation: the throttling share is essentially unchanged from 12:12:36 to 12:54:36, so it does not explain an onset inside the window.

gaps: The RequestErrorRate alerting rule is not loaded in the Prometheus that was queried: list_prometheus_rules returned no_data both for rule_name RequestErrorRate and for {severity="warning"}, so the alert's exact expression, its denominator and the reported 0.01111111111111111 cannot be verified; the ingress error share measured at 12:41:36Z is about 0.037%.

The metric families the alert could be based on are absent from this Prometheus: no http_server_request_duration_seconds_count and no rpc_client_duration_milliseconds_count series exist in the queried window (the http_*/rpc_* name search returned no_data), so those candidate sources could not be tested.

The frontend container produced no readable log lines in the window (fetch_pod_logs for frontend-675fd7b5c5-chsmw over 12:00-12:31Z returned no_data with 0 lines), so whether the frontend application logged a panic, unhandled rejection or timeout before terminating the connections is unknown.

The product-catalog log query over 12:34-12:45Z returned no matching error lines but the view was flagged no_data/incomplete, so absence of application errors in the new product-catalog pod is not established.

frontend-proxy's envoy configuration (upstream idle timeout, max_requests_per_connection, drain behaviour for the 'frontend' cluster) is not available as a Kubernetes object; it is baked into the container image, so the keep-alive/pool hypotheses cannot be confirmed.

Jaeger data for this environment ends around 12:30:06Z (traces_search source_end_at), so the 12:31:36-12:36:36Z spike in frontend-proxy 503s and frontend's own error spans cannot be inspected as traces, and post-12:30 requests are unseen.

frontend-proxy container log reads over 12:02-12:10Z and 12:10-12:20Z were reported no_data/incomplete (read limit reached reading forward from 12:30), so behaviour between pod start at 12:01:10Z and the first logged 503 at 12:11:30.947Z is not fully established.

kube-state-metrics kube_* series (for example kube_pod_owner, kube_deployment_status_replicas_ready) are absent from this Prometheus, so workload status was taken from the Kubernetes API at query time, not from the incident window.

The frontend service's error spans at 12:31:36-12:36:36Z (GET 5.56, POST 1.11, POST /api/checkout 1.11, executing api route /api/checkout 1.11, tcp.connect 1.11) are not demonstrably the same events as the 503 UC connection terminations: the 503 requests have no frontend span at all, while these are frontend server/internal spans that returned errors.
No change-history integration is available in this Run, so no deployment or configuration change record can be correlated with the 12:11:30Z onset of the 503s.
next_steps: Compare frontend-proxy's envoy cluster configuration for the 'frontend' upstream (common_http_protocol_options.idle_timeout, max_requests_per_connection, HTTP/1 vs HTTP/2) with the frontend Node/Next.js server keepAliveTimeout and headersTimeout, and align them if they are mismatched.
Capture the frontend container's stdout/stderr (and any Next.js server error output) during a repetition of the 503s, since no application log evidence was available.

Retrieve the actual RequestErrorRate rule definition and its numerator/denominator from the Alertmanager/Prometheus that evaluates it, then confirm whether the 1.1% reading comes from a smaller operation-level denominator than the 'ingress' operation used here.
Re-check the frontend's CPU limit (currently 100m with 24-32% steady throttling) if request latency or connection churn needs to be reduced; this is advisory and not established as the trigger.
